title: Michael Burry keeps pointing at unloved stocks for a reason

Michael Burry keeps pointing at unloved stocks for a reason

Everyone knows the clearance-rack dilemma. The markdown looks like a steal, yet the empty aisle makes you wonder what others know that you don't.

In a Substack post on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, "Big Short" investor Michael Burry said he added "in some size" to four short bets, Seeking Alpha reported.

They target Micron Technology (MU), Nebius Group (NBIS), Palantir Technologies (PLTR), and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX).

In the same post, he bought more of five stocks sitting 29% to 65% below their 52-week highs. He is shopping the empty aisle while shorting the crowded one.

The 5 stocks Burry now calls full positions

The five stocks Burry highlighted include QXO (QXO), Build-A-Bear Workshop (BBW), Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM), Birkenstock Holding (BIRK), and MercadoLibre (MELI). Burry said all had "corrected tremendously" and are now full positions, according to Seeking Alpha.

Here is where each closed on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026.

Down 56% from its $27.61 high, building-products distributor QXO closed at $12.28, near its $11.14 low, and its 18 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a $29.11 target, according to Stock Analysis.

Down 65% from its $74.38 high, stuffed-animal retailer Build-A-Bear closed at $25.96, according to MacroTrends, after an August outlook cut, Reuters reported. It sits near its $24.15 low, with four analysts rating it Strong Buy at a $43 target, Stock Analysis confirmed.

Down 45% from its $119.98 high, natural grocer Sprouts closed at $66.07, near its $64.75 low, and its 16 analysts rate it Buy with a $95 target, according to Stock Analysis.

Down 38% from its $50.73 high, sandal maker Birkenstock closed at $31.68 on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, near its $29.93 low, and its 23 analysts rate it Buy with a $51.19 target, Stock Analysis noted.

Down 29% from its $2,548.50 high, Latin American e-commerce leader MercadoLibre closed at $1,799.24, above its $1,495 low, and its 24 analysts rate it Buy with a $2,264.88 target, Stock Analysis indicated.

Wall Street agrees with Burry here. All five carry Buy or Strong Buy ratings from analysts polled by S&P Global, with targets implying 26% to 137% upside, according to Stock Analysis.

Prices kept sliding anyway, with QXO and Sprouts each down nearly 4% the next day, based on the same data.

While Burry is doubling down on these beaten-down value plays, his strategy tells a two-sided story. On the other side of the ledger, he is taking aggressive short positions against the market's high-flying AI and tech darlings.

title: Does Palantir Stock Make Your Bad Market Days Worse?
detail:
Does Palantir Stock Make Your Bad Market Days Worse?
Trefis Team
Thu, September 24, 2026 at 8:09 AM MST 3 min read
PLTR
^GSPC
AMZN
IBM
SNOW
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pexels

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) stock has climbed 10.0% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 rose 2.0%. A run like that invites you to chase it. But one week is not the question. The question is what Palantir does to your money when the market moves, because it travels further than the index both ways and further still on the way down.

How Far Does Palantir Carry Your Money When The Market Moves?

On days the S&P 500 rose over the past year, Palantir captured about 206% of the market's gain. On days it fell, Palantir absorbed about 240% of the market's loss. Both are one-year readings, and they can shift.

That makes Palantir leverage on the market, with the losing side the larger one. Over the past five years its annualized volatility was 67.0%, against 17.2% for the S&P 500. That is nearly four times the index's swing.

Not all of that movement is the market's. Over the same five years, Palantir's daily returns tracked the index at a correlation of 0.54, so a good part of what it does is its own. A stock can magnify the market and still swing widely for reasons of its own.

Why Might Palantir Take More Of The Market's Falls Than Its Gains?

The business is not the fragile part. Palantir earns an operating margin of 42.8%, against an S&P 500 median of 18.6%. Its revenue grew 78.9% over the trailing twelve months, against an S&P 500 median of 8.3%.

The fragile part is the price. Palantir trades at 74.8 times sales, while the S&P 500 median is 3.1 times. A price that far ahead of sales depends on growth like this lasting for years. That leaves little room for doubt, which fits a stock that has taken more of the market's falls than its gains over the past year.

In Q2 2026, the U.S. accounted for over 81% of Palantir's revenue, and U.S. commercial revenue growth accelerated as more companies bought the AIP platform to keep full ownership of their data, logic, and security. Management calls this AI sovereignty. That demand is what the price is counting on.

Has Palantir Paid You Enough For The Extra Swing?

Over five years, in raw return, yes. Palantir returned an annualized 46.4%, against 13.2% for the S&P 500.

At its Q2 2026 report in August, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint to $8.154 billion. The Q3 2026 report is the next check on the growth the price assumes. A quarter that keeps Palantir on track for that guide, or raises it again, would support the price. A shortfall would land on a stock that already falls harder than the market.

Enterprise AI is quickly becoming one of technology's biggest battlegrounds. Businesses are no longer experimenting with artificial intelligence just to see what it can do. They are already convinced of its potential and are now looking at how to apply it across their operations. That shift is creating opportunities for software companies that can turn AI into something businesses actually use, rather than another expensive experiment.

Two companies stand out for very different reasons: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and Salesforce (CRM). Both are chasing the same enterprise AI opportunity, but their growth, valuations, and approaches to rewarding shareholders look very different.

For dividend investors, that adds another layer to the comparison, especially since AI growth and shareholder returns don't always go hand in hand.

So which enterprise AI stock offers the better proposition today?

Palantir Powers Data and Defense at a $444 Billion Valuation

Palantir Technologies is an enterprise software company known for its data analysis solutions and its use of artificial intelligence in real-world operations. Many industries use its software, including the U.S. government and defense agencies. The company is the larger of the two, with a market cap of $460 billion.

Salesforce Builds AI Into a $192 Billion CRM Empire

Salesforce is another enterprise software company built around a customer relationship management platform. It helps businesses manage customer relationships and is leaning further into AI through Agentforce, which I'll cover later. Its market cap is $195 billion.

The two companies compete in the same enterprise software market, but Palantir is already worth more than twice as much as Salesforce. But does its business justify that gap?

Palantir vs. Salesforce in the Battle for Enterprise AI

Both companies are betting heavily on enterprise AI, but the drivers behind it are entirely different.

Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform, or AIP, connects AI with a company's existing data and day-to-day operations. Think of it as an advanced chatbot that actually helps with your day-to-day operations. It lets businesses analyze information and make decisions, even automating much of their work.

Shares climbed more than 3% Wednesday and moved above $190, their highest level in nearly a year. The stock has gained 69% over the past three months, helped by stronger-than-expected results and growing adoption of its Artificial Intelligence Platform.

The latest boost came from the U.S. Army, which awarded Palantir a $48.1 million contract to build an enterprise ammunition-management system. The platform will replace nine older systems with a single system.

Palantir is also expanding its work overseas. CEO Alex Karp met with the presidents of Poland and Lithuania this week to discuss potential technology investments, while the company has announced partnerships with Nvidia, Nebius and Method Security. A separate deal with Fujitsu is aimed at expanding Palantir's software across enterprise networks in Japan.

The FAA is another potential source of growth. The agency recently began using Palantir's AI-powered SMART system at three Washington-area airports to identify congestion and other problems before they develop.

Rosenblatt analyst John McPeake reiterated a Buy rating and a $225 price target, citing additional FAA opportunities.

The next catalyst is whether Palantir can turn these new government deployments and partnerships into sustained revenue growth beyond its already rapid expansion.

Prediction: This Will Be Palantir Technologies’ Stock Price by the End of 2028
Harsh Chauhan, The Motley Fool

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) has turned in a disappointing performance on the stock market so far in 2026, with shares of the software specialist rising just 4% compared to the 17% appreciation in the Nasdaq Composite index.

However, the artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist has seen a sharp rise in its stock price recently. Palantir stock is up by 50% since the beginning of August. The good part is that Wall Street expects Palantir to jump higher over the coming year. But can Palantir sustain its newfound momentum beyond that and deliver healthy gains to investors by the end of 2028?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's find out.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Improving confidence in software stocks has powered Palantir's surge

Palantir's poor returns in 2026 can be attributed to a lack of confidence in software stocks. Wall Street was concerned that the growing proliferation of AI would render the software industry redundant, but the sector has bounced back lately. In fact, software stocks have been outperforming semiconductor stocks.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF has gained 22% over the past three months, while the iShares Semiconductor Sector ETF is down 12% over the same period. Palantir has benefited from this rebound, and quite rightly so.

After all, the company has been growing at an incredible pace amid the booming demand for generative AI software by enterprises and governments.

PLTR Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts

Palantir reported a 93% year-over-year increase in revenue in the second quarter to $1.94 billion. Its non-GAAP earnings per share increased by a whopping 156% year over year to $0.41. The company now expects to end 2026 with an 82% increase in revenue to just over $8.15 billion. However, I won't be surprised to see Palantir finishing the year with a bigger revenue increase.

That's because the company has been adding new customers at a nice clip, and those customers tend to spend more on its AI software tools over time. For instance, Palantir management noted on last month's earnings call that a tech company that deployed its solutions in the fourth quarter of 2025 has now entered into a three-year, $370 million deal.

Similarly, many other companies that enter into contracts with Palantir expand their scope of work due to the productivity gains delivered by its AI software platform. This explains why businesses have been giving Palantir sizable contracts. The company's total contract value (TCV) in the U.S. commercial business was up by a stunning 2.5x year over year in Q2 to $2.13 billion, well above the 49% year-over-year jump in the overall TCV to $3.37 billion.

Prediction: This Will Be Palantir's Stock Price by the End of 2028 as Commercial Sales Accelerate

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has been one of the top stocks to buy in the artificial intelligence (AI) arms race. Since 2023, Palantir has risen by more than 2,600%. Although it's unlikely to repeat that performance, many investors are bullish on Palantir's future.

But where will that place the stock by 2028? Let's take a look.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Palantir's growth won't stop accelerating

Palantir has been involved in the AI sector for a long time. It began by providing AI software to government entities and made quite a name for itself in that industry. Eventually, it found a commercial use case for its product and expanded into that area.

This side of Palantir's business has been booming lately, and its government business has also performed well. In Q2, Palantir's U.S. commercial business revenue rose at an incredible 149% rate. Palantir's AI business is booming, but not everyone expected it to do so well.

Few companies have defied expectations like Palantir. For several quarters, Wall Street analysts have forecast that its growth rate would slow. Likewise, Palantir's internal projections also indicated growth may slow, but that has never occurred.

PLTR Revenue (Quarterly YOY Growth) data by YCharts

Palantir's growth rate continues to accelerate, and with the widespread AI demand wave, it will likely continue. However, Wall Street analysts are still forecasting a slowdown. For Q3, they estimate 84% growth. For 2027, they estimate 49% growth.

We will see if its growth rate actually decelerates, but if history has anything to say about this trend, I'd be willing to bet that it won't be that much of a decline. Although I wouldn't be surprised to see Palantir's growth rate decrease somewhat, I doubt it's to the degree that Wall Street is estimating. That would flip analyst projections on their heads, but there's only one problem: Rapid growth is already baked into the stock price.

Palantir's stock price assumes a ton of growth

Palantir is one of the most expensively valued stocks on the market. It trades for more than 150 times earnings.

PLTR PE Ratio data by YCharts

While some tech and growth investors may be used to their stocks trading for sky-high multiples, most of the time, those companies aren't optimized for profits. Palantir is. During its most recent quarter, Palantir posted an impressive 55% profit margin. There's not a lot more room for growth from that perspective, so for Palantir to achieve a reasonable valuation, it must grow its way out of it.
